# Converting ALA/LC transliteration of Russian into Cyrillic. 
# Based on http://www.loc.gov/catdir/cpso/romanization/russian.pdf
# Created by Leonid Taycher (leonid@google.com)
# Rule ordering does not correspond to russian alphabet, since rules needed
# to be reordered because of ICU's first come-first serve interpretation
$upperConsonants = [\u0411\u0412\u0413\u0414\u0416\u0417\u0419\u041a\u041b\u041c
\u041d\u041f\u0420\u0421\u0422\u0424\u0425\u0426\u0427\u0428\u0429\u042a\u042c];
$lowerConsonants = [\u0431\u0432\u0433\u0434\u0436\u0437\u0439\u043a\u043b\u043c
\u043d\u043f\u0440\u0441\u0442\u0444\u0445\u0446\u0447\u0448\u0449\u044a\u044c];
$consonants = [$upperConsonants $lowerConsonants];
$upperVowels = [\u0410\u0415\u0401\u0418\u041e\u0423\u042b\u042d\u042e\u042f];
$lowerVowels = [\u0430\u0435\u0451\u0438\u043e\u0443\u044b\u044d\u044e\u044f];
$vowels = [$upperVowels $lowerVowels]; 
# Skipping roman numerals (usually century numbers, so staying within tens is fine)
(I*V*I*X(I*V?X*I*V?)*) > $1 ;
# Making under-ten transformations explitic
(II) > $1 ;
(III) > $1 ;
(IV) > $1 ;
(VI) > $1 ;
(VII) > $1 ;
(VIII) > $1 ;

[JY][Uu] > \u042e ; # CYRILLIC CAPITAL LETTER YU (not in ALA/LC proper but used)
[jy]u > \u044e ; # CYRILLIC SMALL LETTER YU (not in ALA/LC proper but used)
$vowels { ia > \u044f ; # 'ia' following a vowel is CYRILLIC SMALL LETTER YA (not in ALA/LC proper but used)

$consonants { iu > \u044e ; # After a consonant 'iu' is always SMALL LETTER YU

# Transforms Amharic (am) to Amharic in phonemic IPA transcription (am_FONIPA).
# The International Phonetic Alphabet is described here:
# http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Phonetic_Alphabet#Letters
# In the am 
 am_FONIPA transformation, the following phonemes are produced:
# Pulmonic consonants 
 Nasals:
#     /m/ Bilabial nasal: 
#     /n/ Alveolar nasal: 
#     /
/ Palatal nasal: 
# Pulmonic consonants 
 Stops:
#     /p/ Voiceless bilabial stop: 
#     /b/ Voiced bilabial stop: 
#     /t/ Voiceless alveolar stop: 
#     /d/ Voiced alveolar stop: 
#     /k/ Voiceless velar stop: 
#     /g/ Voiced velar stop: 
#     /
/ Glottal stop: 
# Pulmonic consonants 
 Fricatives:
#     /f/ Voiceless labiodental fricative: 
#     /v/ Voiced labiodental fricative: 
#     /s/ Voiceless alveolar sibilant: 
#     /z/ Voiced alveolar sibilant: 
#     /
/ Voiceless palato-alveolar sibilant: 
#     /
/ Voiced palato-alveolar sibilant: 
#     /
/ Voiced pharyngeal fricative: 
#     /h/ Voiceless glottal fricative: 
# Pulmonic consonants 
 Others:
#     /r/ Alveolar trill: 
#     /j/ Palatal approximant: 
#     /l/ Alveolar lateral approximant: 
# Non-pulmonic consonants:
#     /p
/ Bilabial ejective stop: 
#     /t
/ Alveolar ejective stop: 
#     /k
/ Velar ejective stop: 
#     /s
/ Alveolar ejective fricative: 
# Affricates:
#     /t
/ Voiceless palato-alveolar affricate: 
#     /t
/ Voiceless palato-alveolar ejective affricate: 
#     /d
/ Voiced palato-alveolar affricate: 
# Co-articulated consonants:
#     /w/ Labio-velar approximant: 
# Vowels:
#    /i/ Close front unrounded vowel: 
#    /
/ Close central unrounded vowel: 
/, often but not always silent
#    /u/ Close back rounded vowel: 
#    /e/ Close-mid front unrounded vowel: 
#    /o/ Close-mid back rounded vowel: 
#    /
/ Mid central vowel: 
#    /a/ Open front unrounded vowel:

#     Amharic speakers will usually say

a] instead of [mwa];
#     labializing [m] instead of saying [m] followed by a separate [w].
#     Most Amharic consonants can get labialized. To keep the phonemic

# Buckwalter transliteration of Arabic.  A very simple character substitution
# that can be applied in both directions.
# See http://www.qamus.org/transliteration.htm
# When transliterating from Arabic to Latin, put Arabic into composed normal
# form.  The original Buckwalter transliteration was defined in terms of
# ISO 8859-6, which corresponds to the composed Unicode characters listed below.

# Romanization of Arabic based on the United Nations system.
# Based on the romanization scheme devloped by the United Nations Group of
# Experts on Geographical Names (UNGEGN), Working Group on Romanization Systems
# (WGRS).  See http://www.eki.ee/wgrs/ for background and
# http://www.eki.ee/wgrs/rom1_ar.{htm,pdf} for the UN romanization of Arabic.
# Differences:
# 1) The UN standard is vague on the precise shape of the ayin and hamza
#    transliterated characters.  The present file chooses modifier letters
#    derived from raised or inverted commas.
# 2) The UN standard suppresses hamza at the beginning of a word.  The present
#    file retains it.
# 3) The UN standard transcribes both 
 (KHAH) and 
 (KAF + HEH) as "kh".
#    The present file transcribes 
 as "k
h".  Similarly for "th", "sh", etc.
$wordBoundary = [^[:L:][:M:][:N:]];

$ayin = 
 ;    # nonstandard (turned comma); UNGEGN HTML uses LEFT SINGLE QUOTE
$hamza = 
;    # nonstandard (apostrophe); UNGEGN HTML uses RIGHT SINGLE QUOTE
$al = \uE001;  # private marker for the beginning of the definite determiner
$cdot = 
# Normalize, then transpose SHADDA and harakaat.
# Having the SHADDA immediately follow the consonant it modifies greatly
# simplifies the remaining rules.  Unfortunately, NFC orders the SHADDA after
# the short vowel markers (harakaat).  The rules in this pass undo this.
:: NFC (NFC);
# Isolate the definite determiner "al-".
:: Null();
$wordBoundary { 
 $al a $1 '-' $1;
$wordBoundary { 
 $al a l '-';
# Expand SHADDA.
:: Null();
 $1 $1;
# Romanize.
:: Null();
 $hamza;    # ARABIC LETTER HAMZA
 $hamza 
;  # ARABIC LETTER ALEF WITH MADDA ABOVE
 $hamza;    # ARABIC LETTER ALEF WITH HAMZA ABOVE
 $hamza u;  # ARABIC LETTER WAW WITH HAMZA ABOVE  # check transcription
 $hamza;    # ARABIC LETTER ALEF WITH HAMZA BELOW
 $hamza i;  # ARABIC LETTER YEH WITH HAMZA ABOVE  # check transcription
# ARABIC LETTER ALEF
# ARABIC LETTER TEH MARBUTA
 } [$harakaat] 
# ARABIC LETTER WAW
 } [^ $harakaat] 
# ARABIC LETTER ALEF MAKSURA
# ARABIC LETTER YEH

# Regressive assimilation: out of two successive consonants,
# the first takes the voicedness of the second.
# - (p, t, k, ty, sz, s, c, cs, f) becomes voiced before
#   (b, d, g, gy, z, dzs)
# - (b, d, g, gy, z, zs, dz, dzs, v) becomes unvoiced before
#   (p, t, k, ty, sz, s, c, cs, f, h)
$voiced = [bd
z];  # d matches d
. Also d
z, but no words start with d
$unvoiced = [ptkcs
fh];  # t matches t
s and t

# The previous rules produced geminates.
# Repeat most degemination rules in a new phase,
# so the following rules apply.

$consonant t
$consonant d

{k} $voiced 
{c} $voiced 
{s} $voiced 
} $voiced 
s} $voiced 
} $voiced

} $unvoiced

{v} $unvoiced 
# Progressive assimilation: j becomes unvoiced (ich-Laut)
# at the end of a word if it follows p, k or f.
[pkf] {j} [$] 
# Some phonetic rules are not implemented:
# - h at the end of syllables is mute, but there are many exceptions.
#   Example: mute in m
h, not mute in ihlet.
# - intercluster elision: middle alveolar stops may be omitted in
#   clusters of three or more consonants,
#   depending on speed and articulation of speech.
# Copyright 2010 Google Inc. All Rights Reserved.
# Author: mjansche@google.com (Martin Jansche)
# Conversion between IPA and X-SAMPA phonetic transcription.
# See http://www.phon.ucl.ac.uk/home/sampa/x-sampa.htm for a description of
# X-SAMPA, an ASCII encoding of the International Phonetic Alphabet.
# The following obsolete or extended IPA symbols have no X-SAMPA equivalents
# and remain unaffected by this transform:
  LATIN SMALL LETTER TURNED K
  LATIN SMALL LETTER FENG DIGRAPH
  LATIN SMALL LETTER LS DIGRAPH
  LATIN SMALL LETTER LZ DIGRAPH
  LATIN LETTER BILABIAL PERCUSSIVE
  LATIN LETTER BIDENTAL PERCUSSIVE
# An IPA tie bar is transformed to an X-SAMPA underscore, per the official
# X-SAMPA guidelines.  This can result in certain ambiguities: For example, the
# labial-velar nasal (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labial-velar_nasal) can be
# either written as [
m] or [m
] in IPA.  However, neither version can be
# represented unambiguously in X-SAMPA: IPA [
m] becomes X-SAMPA [N_m], which
# is also used to represent a hypothetical laminal (_m) velar nasal, IPA [
# and IPA [m
] becomes X-SAMPA [m_N], which can also represent a linguolabial
# (_N) nasal, IPA [m
], which is more appropriately written [n
].  To avoid
# unintended ambiguities, it may therefore be advisable to write affricates
# without tie bars.
$t = '_';  # X-SAMPA representation of IPA tie bar.

# Description: Khmer to Latin Transliteration
::[[:Khmer:][:block=KHMER:]\u200B[:P:]];
::NFKD(NFC);
# Khmer uses a complex script where a single character is composed of
# multiple unicode codepoints. The first codepoint is typically a
# consonant, followed by one or more consonants and vowels.  The
# pronunciation of vowels is ambiguous and in most cases depends on
# the preceding consonants and vowels.
# The consonants can be divided in two groups called "a-series" and
# "o-series". The vowel pronunciation is different when following
# a-series consonants and o-series consonants. There are also
# exceptions that explicitly or implicitly change vowel pronunciation.
# There is also agreement of vowel pronouncement across syllables
# within words (vowel harmony). The second vowel pronounciation has to
# agree with the previous vowel. E.g. if the previous vowel was from
# the a-series, the current vowel has to be from the a-series
# Vowel harmony is currently not handled in this ruleset.
# Coeng is a non-printing symbol that indicates that the following
# symbol is a subscript.
$coeng = [\u17D2];
# Muusikatoan character forces a-series on the following vowel
$muusikatoan = \u17C9;
# Treisap character forces o-series on the following vowel
$treisap = \u17CA;
$vowels = [\u17A3-\u17C5aeiou];
$consonants = [\u1780-\u17A2];
$nonconsonants = [^\u1780-\u17A2];
# List of o-series consonants including treisap
$oseries = [\u1782-\u1784\u1787-\u1789\u178C-\u178D\u1791-\u1793\u1796-\u179C\u17CA];
# List of a-series consonants including muusikatoan
$aseries = [\u1780\u1781\u1785\u1786\u178A\u178B\u178E\u178F\u1790\u1794\u1795\u179D\u179F-\u17A2\u17C9];
# First, dealing with word boundary
::Any-BreakInternal;
# Many web page also use zwsp to mark word boundary. Turn zwsp into space

# some hardcoded exceptions where Sanskrit/Pali reading applies instead of plain Khmer
 > akthireach;
# Exceptions for harmony of U+17B6
 > karngear;
# Vowel insertion after consonant sequences
($aseries $coeng $consonants) } $consonants > | $1 a;
($oseries $coeng $consonants) } $consonants > | $1 o;
# Special treatment of U+179A (RO) in a consonant cluster at the end of words
# consonants removed at the end of words
$consonants { ($coeng $consonants) } [$] > ;

# ($aseries $coeng* $consonants* $vowels*  $consonants*) ($oseries $coeng* $consonants*) (

# Transforms Kinyarwanda (rw) to its IPA transcription (rw_FONIPA).
# Kinyarwanda has tones, and vowel length is phonemically distinctive.
# Our simplistic transforms are not able to generate these distinctions,
# so the quality of the output is rather 
 and would need to be
# supplemented by a large exception dictionary for most applications.
# http://www.laits.utexas.edu/phonology/kinyarwanda/
# http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinyarwanda
::NFC;
::Lower;
$word_boundary = [-\ $];
{a} $word_boundary 
[aeiou] {bw} 
;  # eg. ubwenge
;   # eg. bwinshi
;  # according to http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinyarwanda#Orthography
kw; # according to http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinyarwanda#Orthography
 dgw;  # according to http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinyarwanda#Orthography
{eye} $word_boundary 
;  # eg. ukomeye, akomeye
{e} $word_boundary 
{g} [ei] 
 {i} $word_boundary 
;  # eg. umugi, igi
{i} $word_boundary 
{k} [ei] 
 mb;   # eg. imbogo, igikombe
;   # eg. umwana, umwami, umwanya
;   # eg. iryamye
{ng} [ei] 
;   # eg. ubwenge
;   # eg. umuganga, ingurube
;   # eg. umuntu
;    # eg. gukenyera, umwanya
{o} $word_boundary 
 pk;   # according to http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinyarwanda#Orthography
;  # according to http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinyarwanda#Orthography
 tkw;  # according to http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinyarwanda#Orthography
{u} $word_boundary 
 j;     # eg. zicaye

# This file fills a gap in the standard ICU transliteration of Malayalam, which
# currently fails to transliterate chillu characters properly. (b/18078450)
# After ICU has been updated to include these transliterations, this rule file
# and its associated use in google3/i18n/translit (cl/78362947) can be removed.
# The current (ver. 54.1) ICU Malayalam transilterator skips singlecode-point
# chillus.  When Chillus are represented in the old, deprecated way, using a
# sequence of code points ending with a zero-width joiner, they are
# transliterated, though the zero-width joiner is preserved in the Romanized
# output, e.g.:
 (U+0D7C) is not transliterated.
 (U+0D30 U+0D4D U+200D) is transliterated as "r
" (U+0072 U+200D)
# You can try the current ICU transliterator on their demo page here, to see
# if support for chillus has improved:
# http://demo.icu-project.org/icu-bin/translit
# First pass: convert any old-style multi-code-point chillus to the
# single-code point, for uniform handling.  This is needed because the current
# ICU transliteration of multi-code-point chillus leaves the zero-width joiner
# (U+200D) in the Latin result
; # CHILLU NN U+0D23 U+0D4D U+200D 
 U+0D7A
;  # CHILLU N  U+0D28 U+0D4D U+200D 
 U+0D7B

 U+0D7C
;  # CHILLU L  U+0D32 U+0D4D U+200D 
 U+0D7D
;   # CHILLU LL U+0D33 U+0D4D U+200D 
 U+0D7E
;  # CHILLU K  U+0D15 U+0D4D U+200D 
 U+0D7F
# Reset to the beginning of the string, so the chillu rules below will apply to
# any single-code-point chillus added by the first pass.
::Null;
# Second pass: transliterate the chillus.
# Everything else is handled by the current ICU Malayalam transliterator.

# Convert from PinYin Used in PR China to BoPoMoFo used in Taiwan
# Input: Pinyin
# Output: BoPoMoFo
#  Notice in Pinyin the tone mark are encoded as Combining Diacritical Marks
#  where the 
#    first tone:   \u0304 Combining Macron in decomposed form
#    second tone:  \u0301 Combining Acute Accent in decomposed form
#    third tone:   \u0306 Combining Breve in decomposed form
#    forth tone:   \u0300 Combining Grave Accent in decomposed form
#    light tone:   no mark
# but in BoPoMoFo the tone mark are encoded as Spacing Modifier Letters
#    first tone:   SPACE
#    second tone:  \u02ca Modifier Letter Acute Accent
#    third tone:   \u02c7 Caron
#    forth tone:   \u02cb Modifier Letter Grave Accent
#    light tone:   \u02d9 Dot Above

# Post-processing code for Hindi romanization
# Get ready to work on some accents.
::NFD;
# n with macron goes to just 'n'
n \u0304 > n ;
# fix up long and short 'e'
e \u0304 > e ;
e > ai ;
# fix up long and short 'o'
o \u0304 > o ;
# u with macron was DEVANAGARI LETTER UU, which should transliterate as 'oo'
u \u0304 > oo ;
# i with macron goes to "ee"
i \u0304 > ee ;
# For any other letter that has a macron on it, double that letter.
([:Letter:]) \u0304 > $1 $1 ;
# Change an m with COMBINING DOT ABOVE to an 'n'.
m \u0307  > n ;
# Same with COMBINING CANDRABINDU.
m \u0310  > n ;
# map both 
 to sh
s \u0323 > sh ; # s with COMBINING DOT BELOW
s \u0301 > sh ; # s with COMBINING ACUTE ACCENT
# map 
 (produced from DHA, DDHA, and DDDHA) to d
r \u0323 > d ; # r with COMBINING DOT BELOW
# Every time we got 'c', it must have come from DEVANAGARI LETTER CA or
# DEVANAGARI LETTER CHA. We want CA to map to 'ch' and CHA to map to 'chh', so
# just change every 'c' to 'ch'.
c > ch ;
# JA with DEVANAGARI SIGN VIRAMA followed by NYA should be "gy" not "j
jn \u0303 > gy ;
# Remove any remaining accents.
::[:Nonspacing Mark:] Remove;
::NFC;
# remove "'" which is not usually typed by users.
\' > ;
# Use this $wordBoundary until bug 2034 is fixed in ICU:
$wordBoundary =  [^[:L:][:M:][:N:]] ;
# Remove word-final 'a' when the word is longer than 2 characters long.
[:Letter:] [:Letter:] { a } $wordBoundary > ;

## Orthographic rules prevent words from ending in a fatha tanween (fathatan)
## unless it is on an alif, hamza, or ta marbuta. In such cases
## an alif is tacked on and the fatha tanween may or may not be moved
## In case the fatha tanween stays put, the fatha tanween-alif sequence
## should still be pronounced as a regular fathatan
 } $wordBoundary > 'an' ;

## TEH MARBUTA goes to empty string, if it's the last letter in a sentence.
## Strictly speaking, it's a syntactic issue whether this is pronounced, but
## for know "end of a sentence" is close enough.
$eos = [[:Sentence_Break=STerm:][:Sentence_Break=ATerm:]
        [:Sentence_Break=CR:][:Sentence_Break=LF:]
        [:Sentence_Break=Sep:][:Sentence_Break=Close:]] ;
## Match TEH MARBUTA next to an end of sentence marker
 } (' ')* $eos > ;
## ... or next to the end of string.
 } (' ')* $ > ;

# Special cases for words with widely-used or idiosyncratic romanizations. Here
# in preprocessing, we write things that we don't want to be changed by the
# postprocessor in ALL CAPS so that postprocessing rules won't fire on them. The
# last step of postprocessing is to lowercase.
